result.topic_en: Examples (divisors 77, 89, 105, 223) of Euler's residue algorithm for finding the least exponent x with 2^x − 1 (or 2^n + 1) divisible by a given odd number, with remarks on what fails when the divisor is composite.

Exemplum 6.

§. 15. Sit diuiſor $N=105$; eritque:

$1-105=-104=-2^3\cdot 13$
$-13+105=+92=+2^2\cdot 23$
$+23+105=+128=+2^7\cdot 1.$

Summa exponentium $=12$; ergo $x=12$, et formula $2^{12}-1$ diuiſibilis erit per 105. At quia 105 non eſt numerus primus, non ſequitur, fore $2^6+1$ per 105 diuiſibile. Tantum enim diuidi poteſt per 5; dum altera formula $2^6-1$ diuiſibilis eſt per $3\cdot 7$.

items.quote: Vnde $x=30$; ita vt $2^{30}-1$ ſit ſimpliciſſima forma per 77 diuiſibilis.
items.english: Hence x = 30, so that 2^30 − 1 is the simplest form divisible by 77.

items.quote: ac reuera, cum $2^5+1$ per 11 ſit diuiſibile, etiam $2^{15}+1$ per 11 erit diuiſibile; at vero per 7 diuiſibilis eſt altera formula $2^{15}-1$, quia factorem habet $2^3-1=7$.
items.english: And indeed, since 2^5 + 1 is divisible by 11, 2^15 + 1 will also be divisible by 11; but the other formula, 2^15 − 1, is divisible by 7, because it has the factor 2^3 − 1 = 7.

items.quote: Hinc ergo $x=11$, ſicque formula $2^{11}-1$ diuiſorem habet 89; nulla autem datur formula alterius ſpeciei $2^n+1$.
items.english: Hence therefore x = 11, and so the formula 2^11 − 1 has the divisor 89; but no formula of the other kind, 2^n + 1, is divisible by 89.

items.quote: ergo $x=12$, et formula $2^{12}-1$ diuiſibilis erit per 105.
items.english: Therefore x = 12, and the formula 2^12 − 1 will be divisible by 105.

items.quote: non ſequitur, fore $2^6+1$ per 105 diuiſibile. Tantum enim diuidi poteſt per 5; dum altera formula $2^6-1$ diuiſibilis eſt per $3\cdot 7$.
items.english: It does not follow that 2^6 + 1 is divisible by 105. For it can only be divided by 5, while the other formula, 2^6 − 1, is divisible by 3·7.
